questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply **BODMAS**: Solve **Bracket** (34 + 21) = 55.

Perform **Multiplication**: 55 × 2 = 110.

Expression becomes: 86 + 57 − 110 + 63 − 19.

Combine positive terms: 86 + 57 + 63 = 206.

Final calculation: 206 − 110 − 19 = 77.

**∴ The correct answer is 77.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 86 + 57 − (34 + 21) × 2 + 63 − 19

**Method:** Apply the **BODMAS** rule (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

⇒ 86 + 57 − (55) × 2 + 63 − 19

⇒ 86 + 57 − 110 + 63 − 19

⇒ (86 + 57 + 63) − (110 + 19)

⇒ 206 − 129

⇒ 77

**∴ The correct answer is 77.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It defines the order of operations: **Brackets** (), **Of** (powers/roots), **Division** (÷), **Multiplication** (×), **Addition** (+), and **Subtraction** (−).

Types of Brackets

Brackets are solved in the order: **Round brackets** ( ), then **Curly brackets** { }, and finally **Square brackets** [ ].

Addition and Subtraction

While addition and subtraction have the same priority, it is usually safer to **group all positive numbers** and **negative numbers** separately before subtracting.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Solve using **BODMAS**: First divide 33 ÷ 3 = 11 and multiply 22 × 2 = 44. The expression becomes: 89 − 47 + 44 + 11 + 28 − 14. Sum of positive terms: 89 + 44 + 11 + 28 = 172. Sum of negative terms: 47 + 14 = 61. Final result: 172 − 61 = 111. **∴ The correct answer is 111.**

questions.question: The time taken to paint a wall is directly proportional to its area. If it takes 6 hours to paint a wall of size 20 m x 15 m, how much time will be required to paint another wall of size 30 m x 20 m?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Area** of Wall 1 = 20 × 15 = 300 m²

**Area** of Wall 2 = 30 × 20 = 600 m²

Since **Time** ∝ **Area**, the area doubles (300 to 600), so time also doubles.

Required Time = 6 × 2 = 12 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Dimensions of **Wall 1** = 20 m × 15 m, **Time₁** = 6 hr

Dimensions of **Wall 2** = 30 m × 20 m

**Formula Used:**

**Area** = Length × Breadth

Direct Proportion: **Time₁** / **Area₁** = **Time₂** / **Area₂**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b4454878cc337f7c1da208f8f791bdd241581802239a7bf1b27b59946a0d2e40.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of **Wall 1** (A₁) = 20 × 15 = 300 m²

⇒ Area of **Wall 2** (A₂) = 30 × 20 = 600 m²

⇒ According to **Direct Proportion**:

⇒ 6 / 300 = **Time₂** / 600

⇒ **Time₂** = (6 × 600) / 300

⇒ **Time₂** = 6 × 2

⇒ **Time₂** = 12 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 12 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Variation

When two quantities are related such that an increase in one results in a proportional increase in the other, it is direct variation (y = kx).

Work-Time Relation

For constant efficiency, work done is directly proportional to time. Formula: W₁/T₁ = W₂/T₂.

Chain Rule

General formula for work: (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) / W₂, where W represents the amount of work (area here).

questions.question: A bus covers a certain distance at a uniform speed. If the speed had been 10 km/h more, it would have taken 1 hour less to cover the same distance. If the original speed was 40 km/h, find the distance covered.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Speed = 40 : (40 + 10) = 40 : 50 = 4 : 5.

Since **distance** is constant, the ratio of Time = 5 : 4.

Difference in time units = 5 − 4 = 1 unit.

Given that 1 unit = 1 hour, so original time = 5 units = 5 hours.

Total **distance** = Original Speed × Original Time = 40 × 5 = 200 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 200 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Original **speed** (s₁) = 40 km/h

Increased **speed** (s₂) = 40 + 10 = 50 km/h

Time difference (Δt) = 1 hour

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c74c465d001df6727b26eb6ee28985d17b2280f0917edc40be7f0c299dc4d42e.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Distance = [ (s₁ × s₂) / (s₂ − s₁) ] × Δt

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance = [ (40 × 50) / (50 − 40) ] × 1

⇒ Distance = [ 2000 / 10 ] × 1

⇒ Distance = 200 × 1

⇒ Distance = 200 km

**∴ The correct answer is 200 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Distance Relationship

Speed is inversely proportional to time when **distance** is constant (S ∝ 1/T). If speed increases, time decreases by the same factor.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time. For two equal distances covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy / (x + y).

questions.question: A laboratory bottle contains 60 ml of a 70% concentration saline solution. 12 ml of the solution is withdrawn and replaced with 12 ml of pure water. Then, 15 ml of the resulting solution is withdrawn and replaced with 15 ml of pure water. What is the final concentration of saline (in percentage) remaining in the bottle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Remaining fraction of saline = (1 − 12/60) × (1 − 15/60)

Remaining fraction = (4/5) × (3/4) = 3/5

Final concentration = Initial concentration × Remaining fraction

Final concentration = 70% × 3/5 = 14% × 3 = 42%

**∴ The correct answer is 42%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial volume (V) = 60 ml

Initial **concentration** = 70%

First replacement volume (x₁) = 12 ml

Second replacement volume (x₂) = 15 ml

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c3b0ccdb80320a25b76cfd051be955482220ad5fd8943ed37e8ad7a2a5efeb61.png] 

**Formula:**

Final Concentration = Initial Concentration × (1 − x₁/V) × (1 − x₂/V)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Final Saline % = 70 × (1 − 12/60) × (1 − 15/60)

⇒ Final Saline % = 70 × (1 − 1/5) × (1 − 1/4)

⇒ Final Saline % = 70 × (4/5) × (3/4)

⇒ Final Saline % = 70 × (3/5)

⇒ Final Saline % = 14 × 3 = 42

**∴ The correct answer is 42%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Removal and Replacement Formula

If a container contains V units of liquid from which x units are taken out and replaced by water, after n operations, the quantity of pure liquid = V × (1 − x/V)ⁿ.

Concentration Ratio

Concentration of a solution is the ratio of solute to the total volume of the solution, often expressed as (Solute Volume ÷ Total Volume) × 100.

Successive Changes

When different volumes are withdrawn, the net reduction factor is the product of individual remaining fractions: (1 − x₁/V) × (1 − x₂/V) × ... × (1 − xₙ/V).

questions.question: Which of the following is smaller than (7/12)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the target fraction 7/12 to have the **common denominator** of 24 (the largest denominator in the options).

7/12 = (7 × 2) / (12 × 2) = 14/24.

Now, compare the numerators: 13/24 has a **smaller numerator** (13) than 14/24 (14).

All other options (2/3 = 16/24, 5/8 = 15/24, 11/8 > 1) are **greater than** 14/24.

**∴ The correct answer is 13/24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Target fraction = 7/12.

**Formula Used:** To compare fractions, convert them to **decimals** or a **common denominator**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2b66d2f445fb851642e7c88aeee3435c3fe0c478eac4b5cbe0c64f99693310cd.png] 

Step 1: Convert the target fraction to a decimal.

⇒ 7/12 = 7 ÷ 12 ≈ 0.5833

Step 2: Convert the options to decimals for **comparison**.

⇒ Option 1: 2/3 = 0.6666 (Larger than 0.5833)

⇒ Option 2: 5/8 = 0.625 (Larger than 0.5833)

⇒ Option 3: 11/8 = 1.375 (Much larger than 1)

⇒ Option 4: 13/24 = 13 ÷ 24 ≈ 0.5416 (Smaller than 0.5833)

⇒ Comparing 0.5416 and 0.5833, we find 0.5416 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cross-Multiplication Method

To compare two fractions a/b and c/d, check the product ad and bc. If **ad < bc**, then a/b < c/d.

Common Denominator Rule

When denominators are equal, the fraction with the **smaller numerator** is the smaller fraction.

Proper vs. Improper Fractions

A **proper fraction** (numerator < denominator) is always smaller than an **improper fraction** (numerator ≥ denominator).

questions.question: The product of the three consecutive odd numbers is 4845. Which is the smallest of the three numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Estimate the **middle term** by finding the **cube root** of the product: √³4845.

Since 16³ = 4096 and 17³ = 4913, the middle odd number must be **17**.

The three **consecutive odd numbers** are (17 − 2), 17, and (17 + 2), which are **15, 17, and 19**.

Verify the product: 15 × 17 × 19 = 255 × 19 = **4845**.

The **smallest** number among them is **15**.

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Product of three consecutive odd numbers = **4845**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a0aba988ae56dea8236bde726c36e07027ebd25f7af0c1e545a000528d4dbe49.png] 

Perform **prime factorization** of 4845 to identify the odd factors:

⇒ 4845 ÷ 5 = 969

⇒ 969 ÷ 3 = 323

⇒ 323 is not divisible by 3, 5, 7, 11, or 13. Testing 17:

⇒ 323 ÷ 17 = 19

⇒ Prime factors are 5, 3, 17, and 19.

⇒ Grouping them into three consecutive numbers: (5 × 3), 17, 19

⇒ Numbers = 15, 17, 19

⇒ Smallest number = 15

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Consecutive Odd Numbers

Consecutive odd numbers always have a **common difference of 2** and can be represented as n, n+2, n+4...

Factorization Rule

When the product of consecutive integers is given, the **middle term** is always close to the **nth root** of the product.

Sum of Consecutive Odd Numbers

The sum of **n** consecutive odd numbers starting from 1 is always a perfect square, given by **n²**.

questions.question: The sum of a positive number and its cube is 350. What is the value of the number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the nearest **perfect cube** to 350.

We know that 7³ = 343 and 8³ = 512.

Testing x = 7: Sum = 7³ + 7 = 343 + 7 = 350.

Since the sum matches 350, the **required number** is 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The sum of a **positive number** and its **cube** is 350.

Let the number be x.

**Formula Used:** x³ + x = 350

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b34c6d3108ab202051ed9271e96c8dce1a75fbf8732c8816c37e425262e4b004.png] 

⇒ x³ + x − 350 = 0

⇒ By **Trial and Error** method, we test the value x = 7.

⇒ 7³ + 7 = 343 + 7

⇒ 350 = 350

⇒ The **Left Hand Side (LHS)** equals the **Right Hand Side (RHS)**.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cubic Equation Properties

A **cubic equation** x³ + ax + b = 0 has at least one real root. For positive x, the function f(x) = x³ + x is **strictly increasing**, meaning it has only one positive solution.

Perfect Cubes

Memorizing **cubes** up to 10 is essential: 5³ = 125, 6³ = 216, 7³ = 343, 8³ = 512, 9³ = 729.

Rational Root Theorem

Potential **integer roots** of a polynomial are always **factors** of the constant term (in this case, factors of 350 like 1, 2, 5, 7, 10, etc.).

questions.question: 38² + 41² - 29² - 36² = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Difference of Squares** identity **a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)** by pairing terms: (38² − 36²) + (41² − 29²).

(38 − 36)(38 + 36) + (41 − 29)(41 + 29)

⇒ 2 × 74 + 12 × 70

⇒ 148 + 840 = 988

**∴ The correct answer is 988.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** 38² + 41² − 29² − 36²

Calculate the **Squares** of the numbers individually:

⇒ 38² = 1444

⇒ 41² = 1681

⇒ 29² = 841

⇒ 36² = 1296

Substitute the squared values back into the expression:

⇒ 1444 + 1681 − 841 − 1296

Group the **Addition** and **Subtraction** terms:

⇒ (1444 + 1681) − (841 + 1296)

⇒ 3125 − 2137

⇒ 988

**∴ The correct answer is 988.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identities for Squares

Standard identities like **(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²** and **a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)** are essential for solving complex arithmetic quickly.

BODMAS Rule

Always solve expressions in the order of **Brackets, Orders (Powers/Roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction**.

Fast Calculation Tips

Memorizing **Squares up to 50** and **Cubes up to 20** helps in reducing the time spent on basic calculations during competitive exams.

questions.question: The area of a square is 36 square cm. What is the perimeter (in cm) of the square?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Side of the **square** = √Area = √36 = 6 cm.

**Perimeter** of the square = 4 × Side = 4 × 6 = 24 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Area of the **square** = 36 cm²

**Formula Used:**

Area of a square = (Side)²

Perimeter of a square = 4 × Side

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/db3ee83863e9e782592ed632531e621dcb153926a0bf581e43c3e7a133eee1a8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = Side²

⇒ 36 = Side²

⇒ Side = √36

⇒ Side = 6 cm

⇒ Perimeter = 4 × Side

⇒ Perimeter = 4 × 6

⇒ Perimeter = 24 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Diagonal of a Square

The diagonal (d) of a square with side (s) is given by d = s√2.

Area using Diagonal

The area of a square can also be calculated using its diagonal as Area = d² ÷ 2.

Properties of a Square

All sides are equal, all interior angles are 90°, and diagonals bisect each other at 90°.

questions.question: The area of a square is 144 square cm. What is the diagonal (in cm) of the square?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The relationship between the **Area** and the **Diagonal** (d) of a **square** is: **Area** = d² ÷ 2.

⇒ 144 = d² ÷ 2

⇒ d² = 144 × 2 = 288

⇒ d = √288 = 12√2 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 12√2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: **Area of the square** = 144 cm²

Formula used: **Area** = (side)² and **Diagonal** = side × √2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2898b50a20188e5c2151550ca1a8e49c6187ca6ea94799377a97257968033af8.png] 

⇒ Side² = 144

⇒ Side = √144

⇒ Side = 12 cm

⇒ **Diagonal** of a square = side × √2

⇒ **Diagonal** = 12 × √2 = 12√2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12√2 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perimeter of a Square

The total boundary length of a square is calculated as 4 × side.

Area in terms of Diagonal

The **Area** of a square can be expressed as 1/2 × (Diagonal)².

Properties of Diagonals

In a **square**, both diagonals are equal in length and bisect each other at right angles (90°).

questions.question: The perimeter of a rectangle is 40 cm. The length of the rectangle is 12 cm. What is the breadth (in cm) of the rectangle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **Rectangle**, the sum of **Length** and **Breadth** is always half of the **Perimeter**.

L + B = Perimeter ÷ 2

12 + B = 40 ÷ 2 = 20

B = 20 − 12 = 8 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Perimeter** of the rectangle = 40 cm

**Length** (L) of the rectangle = 12 cm

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter (P) = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/78cd9f3f7f0edcae1cabf5b2c8b9647acfbcdea81265b3c49056cdd1e1ee5476.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 40 = 2 × (12 + B)

⇒ 40 ÷ 2 = 12 + B

⇒ 20 = 12 + B

⇒ B = 20 − 12

⇒ B = 8 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Rectangle

The total space occupied by the rectangle is calculated as **Area = Length × Breadth**.

Diagonal of a Rectangle

The distance between opposite corners is found using Pythagoras theorem: **d = √(L² + B²)**.

Perimeter of a Square

For a **Square**, all sides (a) are equal, so the **Perimeter = 4 × a**.

questions.question: 11² + 12² + 13² + ...... + 25² = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Required sum = (**Sum of squares** of first 25 **natural numbers**) − (Sum of squares of first 10).

Using **formula** Σn² = [n(n + 1)(2n + 1)] ÷ 6.

Sum(1 to 25) = [25 × 26 × 51] ÷ 6 = 5525.

Sum(1 to 10) = [10 × 11 × 21] ÷ 6 = 385.

Result = 5525 − 385 = 5140.

**∴ The correct answer is 5140.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 11² + 12² + 13² + ... + 25²

**Formula Used:** The **sum of squares** of first **n** natural numbers is Sₙ = [n(n + 1)(2n + 1)] ÷ 6.

⇒ Required value = (1² + 2² + ... + 25²) − (1² + 2² + ... + 10²)

⇒ S₂₅ = [25 × (25 + 1) × (2 × 25 + 1)] ÷ 6

⇒ S₂₅ = (25 × 26 × 51) ÷ 6 = 5525

⇒ S₁₀ = [10 × (10 + 1) × (2 × 10 + 1)] ÷ 6

⇒ S₁₀ = (10 × 11 × 21) ÷ 6 = 385

⇒ Final Sum = 5525 − 385 = 5140

**∴ The correct answer is 5140.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of first n natural numbers

The sum of first **n** natural numbers is given by the formula Σn = [n(n + 1)] ÷ 2.

Sum of cubes of first n natural numbers

The sum of cubes Σn³ is equal to the **square** of the sum of the first **n** numbers: [[n(n + 1)] ÷ 2]².

Sum of first n odd numbers

The sum of the first **n** odd natural numbers (1 + 3 + 5 + ... up to **n** terms) is simply **n²**.

Sum of squares of first n even numbers

The sum of squares of the first **n** even numbers (2² + 4² + ... + (2n)²) is [2n(n + 1)(2n + 1)] ÷ 3.

questions.question: The average expenditure of R for 5 days is Rs. 220. His expenditure for the first 4 days is Rs. 220, Rs. 175, Rs. 185 and Rs. 190 respectively. What is his expenditure (in Rs.) on the 5th day?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume the **average expenditure** of 220 as the base value.

Calculate **net deviation** for the first 4 days: (220−220) + (175−220) + (185−220) + (190−220) = 0 − 45 − 35 − 30 = **−110**.

To keep the **average** constant at 220, the **5th day** must compensate for this negative deviation.

**Expenditure** on 5th day = 220 + 110 = 330.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹330.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Average expenditure** for 5 days = ₹220

**Expenditures** for first 4 days = ₹220, ₹175, ₹185, and ₹190

**Formula Used:**

Total Sum = Average × Number of observations

Value of nth item = Total Sum − Sum of (n−1) items

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/40a33437045667750cc481152696ae712900252f1d56e8f27a2bb0fd5582401d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total expenditure** for 5 days = 220 × 5 = ₹1100

⇒ Sum of **expenditure** for first 4 days = 220 + 175 + 185 + 190

⇒ Sum of 4 days = ₹770

⇒ **Expenditure** on the 5th day = Total expenditure − Sum of 4 days

⇒ 5th day = 1100 − 770

⇒ 5th day = ₹330

**∴ The correct answer is ₹330.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Concept of Average

The **average** (Arithmetic Mean) is the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations. Formula: Average = Σx ÷ n.

Net Deviation Method

In any set of numbers, the **algebraic sum of deviations** from the mean is always zero. This property is used to find a missing value quickly without calculating the total sum.

Change in Average

If a new observation is added, New Sum = (Old Average × Old n) + New Observation. The **new average** then becomes (New Sum) ÷ (n + 1).

questions.question: Average of 13 consecutive natural numbers starting with 'a' is x. What will be the average of 13 consecutive natural numbers starting with 'a + 7'?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any set of numbers, if **every number** in the set is increased by a constant **k**, the **new average** will also increase by **k**.

The first sequence starts at **a** and the second sequence starts at **a + 7**, meaning each of the **13 consecutive numbers** has increased by exactly **7**.

Since the initial average is **x** and the increase per term is **7**, the new average is **x + 7**.

**∴ The correct answer is x + 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of terms (n) = **13**

First sequence starts with **a**. Average = **x**

Second sequence starts with **a + 7**.

**Formula Used:**

Average of **consecutive numbers** = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/930e1fb1c96b096f6097a0fe748ce72281a475ff427c447ca48c7bc631d1f9b4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ For the first sequence: **a, a+1, a+2, ..., a+12**

⇒ Average **x** = (a + a + 12) ÷ 2

⇒ **x** = (2a + 12) ÷ 2 = **a + 6**

⇒ For the second sequence: **(a + 7), (a + 8), ..., (a + 7 + 12)**

⇒ Last term of second sequence = **a + 19**

⇒ New Average = ((a + 7) + (a + 19)) ÷ 2

⇒ New Average = (2a + 26) ÷ 2 = **a + 13**

⇒ Comparing with **x**: New Average = (a + 6) + 7 = **x + 7**

**∴ The correct answer is x + 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of Arithmetic Progression

For any sequence in AP, the average is exactly the **middle term** if the number of terms is odd, or the mean of the two middle terms if even.

Linear Property of Mean

If every observation in a data set is multiplied by **k** and then increased by **c**, the new mean becomes **(Original Mean × k) + c**.

Sum of Natural Numbers

The sum of first **n** consecutive natural numbers is given by the formula: **[n(n + 1)] ÷ 2**.

questions.question: If A percent of A is 729, then what is the value of A²?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If **A percent of A** is given as a value **K**, then the relationship is **A² / 100 = K**.

Here, K = 729.

⇒ A² = 729 × 100 = 72900.

**∴ The correct answer is 72900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The **percentage of a number** itself is given: **A% of A = 729**.

**Formula Used:**

x% of y = (x ÷ 100) × y

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1a3772925662df3f8280dd631f1cad5773bbc940a2cf5b1505ccec73ee301f1e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (A / 100) × A = 729

⇒ A² / 100 = 729

⇒ A² = 729 × 100

⇒ A² = 72900

**∴ The correct answer is 72900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Concept

The term **percent** means **per hundred**. Any value x% is equivalent to the fraction x/100.

Squares of Numbers

The **square** of a number is the result of multiplying the number by itself. For example, if A = 270, then A² = 72900.

Direct Proportion in Percentages

When the **base** and the **percentage rate** are the same (A% of A), the result is always proportional to the **square** of that base divided by 100.

questions.question: The ratio of selling price of an article to the cost price of the article is 13 : 10. What is the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Selling Price (SP)** to **Cost Price (CP)** = 13 : 10

Let **CP** = 10 units and **SP** = 13 units.

**Profit** = SP − CP = 13 − 10 = 3 units.

**Profit percentage** = (Profit / CP) × 100 = (3 / 10) × 100 = 30%.

**∴ The correct answer is 30%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The ratio of **Selling Price (SP)** to **Cost Price (CP)** = 13 : 10

**Formula Used:**

**Profit %** = [(SP − CP) / CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/902b92df0b337ae97cbe6124a22cd1046c566826f40f2b95e0275d00c25e7a6f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let CP = 10k and SP = 13k (where k is a constant)

⇒ **Profit** = 13k − 10k = 3k

⇒ **Profit %** = (3k / 10k) × 100

⇒ **Profit %** = 0.3 × 100

⇒ **Profit %** = 30%

**∴ The correct answer is 30%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

If the **Cost Price** is greater than the **Selling Price**, it is a loss. Loss % = [(CP − SP) / CP] × 100.

Relationship with Marked Price

Profit % can also be related to **Mark-up %** and **Discount %** using the formula: (100 + Profit %) / (100 − Discount %) = MP / CP.

Fractional Conversions

A profit of 30% implies the **multiplier** for CP to reach SP is 1.3 (or 13/10).

questions.question: 12 men can complete (1/2) part of a work in 10 days. How many men can complete 1/3 part of the same work in 20 days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **MDH Formula**: (M₁ × D₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂) / W₂

(12 × 10) / (1/2) = (M₂ × 20) / (1/3)

120 × 2 = M₂ × 60

240 = 60 × M₂ ⇒ M₂ = 4 men

**∴ The correct answer is 4 men.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial men (M₁) = **12 men**, Days (D₁) = **10 days**, Work (W₁) = **1/2 part**

Final men (M₂) = ?, Days (D₂) = **20 days**, Work (W₂) = **1/3 part**

**Formula Used:**

(M₁ × D₁ × E₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × E₂) / W₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3dda3e299aa050f750f96a02df49c1a64d5d9c1f04fcdb789ef4e240d017a068.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (12 × 10) / (1/2) = (M₂ × 20) / (1/3)

⇒ 120 × 2 = M₂ × 20 × 3

⇒ 240 = M₂ × 60

⇒ M₂ = 240 ÷ 60

⇒ M₂ = 4 men

**∴ The correct answer is 4 men.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chain Rule Formula

The general relationship is M₁D₁H₁/W₁ = M₂D₂H₂/W₂, where M is men, D is days, H is hours, and W is work.

Direct and Inverse Proportionality

Number of men is **directly proportional** to work (W ∝ M) and **inversely proportional** to time (M ∝ 1/D).

Work-Rate Logic

Total man-days required for 1 unit of work = (M × D) ÷ Part of work. Here, (12 × 10) ÷ (1/2) = 240 man-days.

questions.question: A takes 5 times as long as B to complete a work. C takes same time as A and B together take to complete a work. A alone can complete a work in 100 days. A, B and C together can complete the same work in how many days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Efficiency ratio** A : B = 1 : 5 (since time ratio is 5 : 1).

Let efficiency of **A** = 1, then efficiency of **B** = 5 and Total Work = 100 units.

Efficiency of **C** = Efficiency (A + B) = 1 + 5 = 6.

Total efficiency (A + B + C) = 1 + 5 + 6 = 12 units/day.

Time taken = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency = 100 ÷ 12 = 25/3 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 25/3 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **A** = 100 days.

Time taken by **A** = 5 × Time taken by **B**.

Time taken by **C** = Time taken by (**A + B**) together.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken by **B** = 100 ÷ 5 = 20 days.

⇒ Let **Total Work** = LCM(100, 20) = 100 units.

⇒ Efficiency of **A** = 1 unit/day.

⇒ Efficiency of **B** = 5 units/day.

⇒ Combined efficiency of **A + B** = 1 + 5 = 6 units/day.

⇒ Since **C** takes the same time as **A + B**, Efficiency of **C** = Efficiency of (**A + B**) = 6 units/day.

⇒ Total efficiency of **A + B + C** = 1 + 5 + 6 = 12 units/day.

⇒ Time taken by **A, B and C** together = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Time = 100 ÷ 12 = 25/3 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 25/3 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken to complete the work. Efficiency = Work ÷ Time.

Combined Efficiency Rule

When multiple people work together, their **individual efficiencies** are added to find the total rate of work.

Work and Wages

Wages are generally distributed in the **ratio of work done** or the **ratio of efficiencies** if they work for the same duration.

questions.question: In a school there are total 300 students. The respective ratio of boys and girls is 3 : 2. 30 more boys gets admitted into the school. What is the total number of boys now in the school?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total units = 3 + 2 = 5 units

5 units = 300 students ⇒ 1 unit = 60 students

Initial **Boys** = 3 × 60 = 180

Total **Boys** now = 180 + 30 = 210

**∴ The correct answer is 210 boys.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of **students** = 300

Ratio of **boys** to **girls** = 3 : 2

Additional **boys** admitted = 30

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/956e144b7a48ef578c392117962fb477b30f953391a70493a91b8c4b104b3369.png] 

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 3 + 2 = 5

⇒ Number of **boys** = (3 ÷ 5) × 300

⇒ Number of **boys** = 3 × 60 = 180

⇒ Number of **girls** = (2 ÷ 5) × 300 = 120

⇒ After admitting 30 more **boys**, new count = 180 + 30

⇒ Total **boys** now = 210

**∴ The correct answer is 210 boys.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio and Proportion

A ratio compares two quantities by division. If a total S is divided in the ratio a:b, the parts are a × S / (a+b) and b × S / (a+b).

New Ratio Calculation

To find the new ratio after an addition, add the extra amount to the specific part. Here, new ratio of Boys:Girls = 210:120 = 7:4.

Percentage of Boys

Initial % of boys = (3/5) × 100 = 60%. After addition, total students = 330, % of boys ≈ 63.63%.
